fullText:
Ministry of Communications

Bharat 6G Alliance Strengthens Global Partnerships at 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026

Union MoS for Communications Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani addresses valedictory session; DoT highlights ESTIC 2026 and its focus on intelligent networks and quantum communication

09 OCT 2026 7:41PM by PIB Delhi

The 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 concluded at Yashobhoomi, Dwarka, New Delhi, with a valedictory address by Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani, Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development. Organised by the Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA) alongside India Mobile Congress 2026, the three-day event brought together global telecom leaders, policymakers, standards organisations, industry, academia and researchers to discuss the roadmap towards IMT-2030 and beyond.

Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development is his address congratulated the Bharat 6G Alliance for organizing the two-day 3rd International Bharat 6G Symposium 2026 and for inviting over 75 speakers, which included more than 30 international experts.

The Union Minister of State said that India is moving from being one of the world’s largest telecom markets to becoming an important telecom technology nation and our indigenous technology journey has taught us something important: Self-reliance and global collaboration are not opposites. The stronger our capabilities, the stronger the partner we can be to the world. The Union Minister of State highlighted that 6G must not create a new digital divide while we are still closing the old one. Affordability, accessibility and coverage must therefore be design requirements — not afterthoughts and in 6G, connectivity need not end where the tower ends. The integration of terrestrial and satellite networks can take connectivity further — to remote villages, islands, oceans and places that traditional networks struggle to reach. India is ready to test these technologies at scale — and share what we learn with the world. Our national goal is Viksit Bharat — a developed India by 2047, the hundredth year of our independence.

The experts contributed to sessions on 5G-Advanced foundations for 6G, global standards, spectrum and WRC-27, international trials and testbeds, AI-native and sustainable networks, startups and academia, global alliances, and industrial use cases. The Symposium emphasized that global interoperability and inclusive 6G development will depend on collaboration across countries, industry, research institutions and standards bodies.

The Symposium reaffirmed India’s commitment to contributing to global 6G research and standards while building indigenous capabilities and strengthening international partnerships. Its discussions called for coordinated standards development, collaborative research, spectrum harmonization and large-scale testing, with affordability, accessibility, security and sustainability embedded in the design of future networks.

A key outcome was the exchange of five new MoUs with GSMA, one6G, GTI Alliance, 6G Innovation Forum (6G IF) Taiwan and VOICE, strengthening opportunities for international cooperation, joint research, trials and knowledge exchange. B6GA also released ten white papers and reports, including a Progress Report on 6G Joint Principles, reflecting continued work towards a 6G ecosystem that is secure, open, resilient, inclusive and sustainable by design.

During the valedictory session in the presence of the Minister of State for Communications, the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) presented a curtain raiser for the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC) 2026. The second edition of this national science and technology platform is scheduled from 27–29 October 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, under the guidance of the Office of the Principal Scientific Adviser and organised by CSIR in collaboration with 12 participating departments/Ministries. Its theme is “Creative Minds, Catalyzing Science, Empowering Technologies”.

The three-day Conclave features plenary talks, 9 thematic technical sessions, panel discussions, presentations by science and technology leaders and deep-tech Startups, exhibitions and B2B/B2G connect meetings.

In the 2nd edition of ESTIC 2026 , DoT is identified to led the thematic session “Intelligent Networks and Quantum Communication”, scheduled for 28 October 2026. The session will explore technologies shaping future digital infrastructure and secure communications. It will feature a keynote by Mr. N. G. Subramaniam, Vice President, TCS; presentations by deep-tech entrepreneurs and technology leaders; and a panel discussion with experts from IIT Kanpur, IIT Delhi, HFCL, Reliance Jio and Bharat 6G Alliance, moderated by Dr. Rajkumar Upadhyay, CEO, C-DOT.

For more details , please visit: www.estic2026.in

About Bharat 6G Alliance

Established in July 2023, Bharat 6G Alliance is an industry-led collaborative platform bringing together telecom service providers, industry, startups, academia and research institutions to advance India’s 6G ambitions. It promotes indigenous research and innovation, intellectual property creation, international standards engagement and partnerships for an affordable, secure, sustainable and globally interoperable 6G ecosystem.

For more details www.bharat6galliance.com

Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Inaugurates Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs at IMC 2026; Highlights Role of Young Innovators in Advancing India’s 5G and 6G Vision

Union Minister Shri Scindia Awards Winners of the 5G Innovation Hackathon

“100 5G Use Case Labs to Nurture Young Innovators and Develop Solutions for India and the World”: Union Minister Shri Scindia

Minister Shri Scindia commends officers of DoT on completion of the specialised Capacity Development Programme on Network and Mobile Security, Distributes Certificates and Badges to them

Initiative aims to transform academic research into practical solutions for India’s next-generation telecommunications ecosystem

Discussions cover AI-native networks, intelligent connectivity, scalable 5G use cases, 6G spectrum roadmap, global standardisation and industry-academia collaboration

09 OCT 2026 7:05PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia inaugurated the Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs at the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026, underscoring the Government of India’s commitment to strengthening indigenous innovation, promoting research and empowering young innovators in the telecommunications sector. Held under the theme “Building Intelligent Networks: Innovations Driving the 5G Advanced and 6G Era,” the workshop aims to foster industry-academia collaboration and accelerate the translation of academic research into practical, technology-driven solutions. The initiative highlights the pivotal role of students, researchers and academic institutions in developing innovative 5G applications and preparing India’s talent ecosystem for next-generation communication technologies.

The workshop also highlighted the importance of bridging the gap between academic research and industry requirements, enabling young talent to contribute to India’s evolving digital and telecommunications landscape. Through these laboratories, students and researchers can explore emerging technologies, experiment with real-world applications and develop solutions with potential benefits across sectors.

“The networks of tomorrow will be imagined not only in exhibition halls but also in our universities, research laboratories and the minds of young innovators. The 100 5G Use Case Labs were established not merely to provide infrastructure, but to nurture innovators capable of developing solutions for India and the world,” said Union Minister Shri Scindia.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Amit Agrawal, Secretary, Department of Telecommunications, emphasised the importance of nurturing innovation beyond conventional infrastructure development and empowering the country’s academic and research ecosystem to shape the future of telecommunications.

The workshop reaffirmed the Government’s focus on fostering collaboration among academia, industry and research institutions to accelerate technology development, promote indigenous solutions and prepare India’s talent pool for the 5G Advanced and 6G era.

By placing young innovators and academic research at the centre of technological advancement, the initiative supports India’s ambition to emerge as a global hub for telecommunications innovation and contribute to the vision of a technologically empowered and self-reliant nation.

Inaugural session features awards distribution to the winners of the 5G Innovation Hackathon (Edition-2) 2026

Addressing the participants at the One-Day Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs, the Union Minister Shri Scindia congratulated the winners of 5G Innovation Hackathon (Edition-2) 2026 and 50 finalists for demonstrating the innovative potential of India’s young talent and encouraged all 1,400 participating teams to continue pursuing new ideas and technological solutions.

Distribution of Certificates to DoT officers Capacity Development Programme

Minister Shri Scindia commended the officers of Department of Telecommunications (DoT), who completed the specialised Capacity Development Programme on Network and Mobile Security. This program included prestigious International certifications like CISSP, CEH, PenTest, CySA etc. Recognising successful completion of the program and their role in strengthening the security of India’s digital infrastructure, Union Minister Shri Scindia distributed the Certificates and Badges to the officers.

Emphasising the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047, the Union Minister underscored the importance of 5G Advanced, 6G and research laboratories in shaping India’s telecommunications future. The Minister called for collaborative efforts to develop intelligent networks that are designed and built in India and trusted globally, and formally declared the One-Day Workshop on 5G Use Case Labs open.

Secretary, DoT congratulated the participating teams and highlighted that innovation should extend beyond competitions and prototypes to intellectual property creation, entrepreneurship, industry partnerships and commercial deployment.

Building Intelligent Networks for Viksit Bharat 2047

The workshop reinforced the importance of connecting academic research, industry requirements and national technology priorities to accelerate India’s transition from technology adoption to indigenous technology development.

The Department of Telecommunications reiterated its commitment to strengthening research, encouraging entrepreneurship and fostering collaboration among academia, startups and industry to advance India’s capabilities in 5G Advanced, 6G and next-generation telecommunications.

About 100 5G Use Case Labs Strengthen India’s Innovation Ecosystem

In October 2023, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi awarded 100 5G Use Case Labs to academic institutions across the country. Established under a Government initiative with an outlay of ₹97.67 crore, all 100 labs became operational by April 2025.

The initiative aims to strengthen practical learning, promote research and development in 5G technologies, encourage industry-academia collaboration and enable startups and micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to access 5G infrastructure for developing innovative applications.

The initiative has delivered encouraging results. By August 2026, more than 17,400 students had utilised the labs, while 97 institutions were conducting 5G courses with over 21,000 students enrolled. The initiative has contributed to the development of 634 products and use cases, with 158 intellectual property filings and 32 patents granted. The participating institutions have also strengthened partnerships with startups, MSMEs and other academic and research organisations.

About 5G Innovation Hackathon 2026

This year, the Hackathon received more than 1,400 proposals across emerging telecommunications domains, including 5G Advanced, artificial intelligence (AI), the Internet of Things (IoT), non-terrestrial networks, Fixed Wireless Access (FWA), network slicing and telecommunications security. The 5G Innovation Hackathon has further strengthened the innovation ecosystem established through the 100 5G Use Case Labs initiative.

Of these, 50 teams were selected and supported with seed funding to develop their ideas. As many as 35 teams are showcasing their innovations at IMC 2026, providing an opportunity to demonstrate their solutions, engage with industry stakeholders and explore avenues for further development and commercialisation.

Ministry of Communications

Union Minister of Communications Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Holds Media Interaction at India Mobile Congress 2026; Calls for Taking Indian Technologies to the World

“The next decade is not to bring the world to India but to take India to the world”: Union Minister Shri Scindia

Union Minister of Communications emphasizes India’s Shift from Digital Connectivity to Global Telecom Technology Leadership at Media Interaction

09 OCT 2026 7:02PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia held a media interaction on the 10th edition of India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2026 highlighting India’s transformation from expanding digital connectivity to developing indigenous technologies and strengthening its position in the global telecommunications ecosystem. The Union Minister emphasised that the next phase of India’s telecom journey would focus on designing, developing and manufacturing technologies in India for domestic and international markets, with closer collaboration between the Government and industry.

Reflecting on the journey of the past decade, the Union Minister said that while the last decade was marked by the expansion of digital connectivity, the next decade must focus on building indigenous technological capabilities, accelerating the deployment of innovations and expanding the global reach of Indian products.

Organised jointly by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT), Ministry of Communications, and the Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI), IMC 2026 is being held at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi under the theme “Scale Without Boundaries”. Highlighting the journey of IMC, Shri Scindia said, “IMC has become Asia’s number one digital and telecom conference at this juncture, and we hope to take it onto a global stage in the days to come.”

IMC 2026: A Global Platform for Technology and Innovation

The scale of the tenth edition is reflected in its 60,000-square-metre exhibition area, participation from over 100 countries, more than 2,000 technology use cases, over 400 startups and more than 900 thought leaders, alongside industry partners, exhibitors, investors, incubators and accelerators. Emphasising that the value of IMC extends beyond participation numbers, Union Minister Shri Scindia noted that its real impact lies in translating ideas into products, partnerships into investments and technological advances into solutions that improve citizens’ lives.

The showcased use cases demonstrate how emerging technologies are moving beyond laboratories and pilot projects into enterprises, public services and everyday applications. The platform also provides opportunities for collaboration among government, industry, academia and the startup ecosystem to accelerate the development, commercialisation and deployment of innovative solutions.

From Connectivity to Indigenous Technology Capability

Union Minister Shri Scindia said that India’s telecom transformation has advanced across three key areas: expanding connectivity, developing indigenous technological capabilities and strengthening domestic manufacturing capacity. The country has expanded broadband infrastructure, undertaken a rapid nationwide 5G rollout, developed an indigenous end-to-end 4G technology stack and strengthened its telecom and electronics manufacturing ecosystem.

Highlighting the country’s evolving ambition, the Union Minister underscored the objective of moving beyond “Made in India” towards “Designed, Developed and Made in India”, while taking Indian technologies and solutions to international markets. This transition reflects India’s growing capacity to design, develop, manufacture and deploy the technologies that underpin digital connectivity, strengthening its position as a technology creator and a trusted global partner.

Union Minister Shri Scindia made special mention of Samriddh Gram, a global award winning initiative of DoT, and demonstrated how digital connectivity and indigenous innovations can support inclusive growth and improve public service delivery. The Samriddhi Kendras under the initiative showcase the potential of integrated digital infrastructure to transform rural communities by connecting government services, healthcare, education, agriculture and local enterprises.

The Union Minister of Communications also highlighted the importance of establishing a seamless pathway from research and intellectual property development to product creation, commercial deployment and access to global markets. Initiatives and institutions such as ASPIRE and C-DOT, along with universities, startups and industry partners, have an important role in strengthening this innovation ecosystem.

The Union Minister concluded the interaction by thanking participating countries, industry partners, exhibitors, startups, innovators, researchers, investors and organisers for contributing to the tenth edition of India Mobile Congress and strengthening its position as a global platform for telecommunications and digital technology collaboration.
